title: Arch- and seq-len-aware kernel pathway cartographer
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: The runtime currently selects kernels using a static cost table keyed by architecture and model family. This leads to suboptimal choices for mixed workloads where per-request sequence length, batch size, and token phase (prefill vs decode) change frequently. Goal: Build a lightweight online "pathway cartographer" that maps device architecture, occupancy, per-request seqlen distribution, and phase to a ranked set of kernel candidates and a warmstart policy. The component should run with minimal overhead, support warm/probing phases, and provide a safe fallback to conservative kernels under SLA pressure.
technical_design: Design summary: 1) Feature vector: {arch_tag, sm_count, engine_version, median_prefill_seqlen, decode_mode_flag, batch_size_hint, kv_cache_hit_rate, timestamp_bucket}. 2) Lightweight cost model: compressed lookup + linearized delta estimator that combines static microbenchmarks with small online observations (latency, tail quantiles). 3) Prober: ephemeral per-machine microprobe that runs single-request microbenchmarks on low-priority background cycles to validate candidate kernels for common seqlen buckets. 4) Warmstart policy: use historical bucketed winners for first N requests, then probe-explore with epsilon=0.05 per bucket. 5) Safety gating: if 95p latency or error rate increases beyond threshold, immediately revert to conservative kernel and mark bucket as degraded. 6) Telemetry: expose per-request kernel_id, latency_buckets, seqlen_bucket, and probe-result events to Console. Implementation notes: keep the cartographer as a runtime library module with a small serialized state per node (~8KB) and offload heavy telemetry aggregation to control plane. Use existing kernel microbench harness to seed static cost table; store per-arch quantized deltas in a compact protobuf for fast lookup.
acceptance_criteria: Cartographer produces a ranked kernel list for requests and integrates with runtime kernel selector API
End-to-end median latency improved by >=6% for mixed seqlen workloads recorded in our benchmark suite
95th percentile latency does not regress more than 2% compared to current conservative baseline under sustained load
Probe overhead <1% CPU on inference nodes and additional memory <16KB per node
Telemetry surfaced in Console with kernel_id, seqlen_bucket, and probe_outcome for every sampled request
Automated canary run demonstrates safe fallback for at least three induced failure scenarios
benchmarks: Mixed-prefill-decode-scenarios fixture (internal perf lab): use 40/60 split prefill/decode across seqlen buckets [8,64,256,1024]
Real-customer replay: 24h sample from two production tenants with heterogeneous seqlen distribution
Tail-latency stress test: 1k concurrent short-decoding requests to validate 95p stability
rollout_plan: 1) Spike + microbench harness updates (branch): profile candidate kernels across representative GPUs
2) Implement cartographer module behind runtime flag; unit + integration tests
3) Canary: enable on 5% of nodes in staging with telemetry sampling at 100%
4) Gradual ramp: 5% -> 25% -> 60% over two weeks while monitoring metrics and automatic rollback triggers
5) Full release with docs and runtime-1.19 release tag if all criteria met
risks: Probe-induced jitter on noisy nodes could affect latency SLOs if not rate-limited
Incorrect seqlen bucketing can cause oscillation between kernels (thrashing)
State drift between nodes if telemetry aggregation lags could lead to inconsistent warmstarts across a request path
mitigations: Rate-limit probes per node and schedule during low-utilization windows
Add hysteresis and minimum dwell time before switching kernel for a bucket
Use centralized heartbeat and periodic reconciliation to ensure node state freshness
